content: I've been thinking about our error handling conventions in Go. We have a mix of sentinel errors, custom error types, and fmt.Errorf wrapping across different services. There's no consistency and it makes debugging harder than it should be.

Inconsistent error handling is one of the most common Go codebase issues. A good starting point is defining a standard error package that all services import, with structured error types that include an error code, message, and cause chain.

That's my plan. I want every error to carry a machine-readable code (like 'PAYMENT_DECLINED' or 'IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT') plus a human-readable message. The code is for programmatic handling, the message is for logs and debugging.

That maps well to how gRPC status codes work — a numeric code plus a message. You could align your error codes with gRPC status codes where they overlap and add domain-specific codes for your business errors.

Good idea. And I want errors to be wrappable — so 'PAYMENT_DECLINED' at the payment service becomes 'PAYMENT_DECLINED: upstream returned insufficient_funds' when it reaches the gateway. Each layer adds context without losing the original code.
Go's error wrapping with %w supports this natively. Your custom error type would implement the Unwrap() method so errors.Is() and errors.As() work through the chain.

Right. The thing is, I also need to make sure these errors serialize cleanly to JSON for our API responses and to our structured logging. One error type, three representations: Go error for internal handling, JSON for API responses, structured log fields for observability.
